books-all-time.issue_summary: The current initial selection has 250 entries and 415 ledger records, of which 369 carry an eligible flag; 132 distinct eligible source IDs appear in current entry references. Seventy-five entries have one source reference, including 58 citing only Modern Library. Ninety-nine eligible records retain generic automatic title/excerpt-review notes and are not linked to current entries. These are audit signals, not proof that every unlinked source is useless or that a full list cannot support many books. The later synthesis preserves an earlier leading group and partly orders additions by website-domain breadth and URL recurrence, which require a clearer distinction from independent comparative judgment.
tasks: Start from every supplied entry, both existing editorial orders and the complete supplied source register. Identify the thinly supported portions of the current pool and conspicuous omissions across literature, philosophy, history, science, religion and other nonfiction; avoid allowing the general books ranking to become a duplicate of literary fiction.

Recheck the source records most material to inclusion and placement. For the 99 eligible records with generic automatic-review notes, distinguish actually examined relevant evidence, useful but unexamined leads, irrelevant material and dependent copies. Record proposed eligibility corrections and their reasons without deleting historical records or claiming fresh consultation merely from the supplied flags.

Map Modern Library, OCLC, Norwegian Book Club/World Library, Goodreads and other recurring list references to their underlying lists and methods. Separate publisher polls, library holdings, reader nominations and independent criticism; identify copied lists and shared dependencies before using recurrence as support.

Use targeted independent criticism, scholarship, editorial selections and substantive reader discussion to resolve consequential coverage or placement gaps. A complete relevant list can support many candidates; do not impose a source-per-entry quota or collect additional URLs solely to raise the total.

Reassess the existing leading group against the whole supported pool instead of treating preserved old positions as fixed. Replace domain/URL breadth as a stand-in for quality with a brief explicit comparative method, recording uncertainty and source disagreement.

Return proposed critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today orders, with concise candidate-specific reasons for consequential changes and for differences between the views. Preserve original source positions separately; leave personal numerical criteria, weights and scores unset.

Resolve work identities, aliases, translations and overlapping collections sufficiently for inclusion. Retain prior entries and evidence in the change history; explain any proposed exclusion or replacement. Record English-edition and image gaps separately so they do not determine merit or block well-supported candidates.
books-all-time.desired_scope: A worldwide, approximately 250-entry ranking of book-length works across subjects. Improve the existing broad pool and both qualitative orders; add or replace entries only with explained scope and evidence, and retain a continuation queue for unresolved candidates.

literature-all-time.issue_summary: The current 250-entry initial selection has 101 eligible ledger records, but only 34 distinct eligible source IDs appear in current entry references. For 231 entries, references are confined to some combination of Modern Library, OCLC Library 100, Penguin reader choices and the Norwegian Book Club poll; 168 entries have a single source reference. Those full lists legitimately support broad candidate discovery, but they offer a narrower basis for worldwide comparative literary standing than the ledger total suggests. The update should improve independent comparative support and scope, not manufacture a larger bibliography.
tasks: Review the full supplied 250-entry pool and both orders against the precise scope of literary fiction. Flag essays, philosophy, nonfiction, plays, individual poems and other out-of-scope forms for an explained decision rather than silently changing the scope or deleting records.

Audit the four dominant list families: Modern Library's selection boundary, OCLC's holdings signal, Penguin's publisher-curated reader choices and the Norwegian Book Club poll. Record each list's original scope, date, source positions and dependencies; do not treat holdings, recommendations and critical judgments as interchangeable evidence.

Distinguish the complete ledger from sources actually supporting current candidates and comparisons. Reuse useful existing scholarly or critical evidence before opening new sources; document target and candidate relevance instead of assigning every source to every book.

Consult targeted independent literary criticism, scholarship, substantial editorial selections and reader discussion where the current pool or ordering depends on one compilation family. Seek missing language traditions and perspectives through reliable relevant sources, without imposing arbitrary geographic or source-family quotas.

Reassess inherited source-list order and the leading group against the full pool. Supply concise work-specific inclusion and placement reasons, including significant disagreements and uncertainty about adjacent positions; avoid using raw recurrence or one list's absent titles as a universal ranking rule.

Return both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today proposals, explaining important differences without equating reading value with ease. Retain prior positions and exact publisher positions as provenance, and leave personal numerical criteria, weights and scores unset.

Normalize alternate titles, author aliases, multi-volume novels, collections and translations. Identify English availability and significant translation issues where evidence allows, keeping detailed edition and image work in a separate unresolved queue rather than an inclusion gate.
literature-all-time.desired_scope: Approximately 250 worldwide literary-fiction works, improving the existing breadth and comparative support. Preserve the two qualitative views and historical evidence; do not pad the list or force particular titles or positions.

nonfiction-all-time.issue_summary: The current initial selection has 250 entries and 322 ledger records; 290 are flagged eligible and 63 distinct eligible source IDs appear in current entry references. There are 111 single-reference entries. Sixty-two entries share exactly S02, OWNER-006 and OWNER-043: the original Modern Library nonfiction list plus two Goodreads presentations of that list, rather than three independent list judgments. A further 147 eligible records retain generic automatic-review notes and are not linked to current entries. The principal needs are dependency correction, broader subject/tradition coverage and better comparative explanations.
tasks: Audit the repeated Modern Library family, beginning with S02, OWNER-006 and OWNER-043. Preserve all source records and original positions, but identify the common underlying list and avoid counting its copied appearances as independent support or multiple votes.

Reassess the 147 eligible records carrying generic automatic title/excerpt-review notes. Return evidence-backed eligibility and dependency corrections, distinguishing supplied prior claims from content you actually consulted; unlinked sources may still contribute valid background or methodology.

Review coverage across history, biography and memoir, science, philosophy, religion, politics, economics, social thought and other eligible nonfiction. Check the influence of Modern Library, TIME, Guardian and curriculum lists on the current pool and identify consequential gaps in languages, traditions or subjects without setting artificial quotas.

Extract useful complete relevant selections and seek targeted independent scholarship, criticism and substantive reader discussion that clarify contested inclusion or placement. Do not treat a university reading sequence as a merit ranking or a source's omission as a negative assessment.

Assess intellectual achievement, historical influence, factual reliability and current reading value distinctly. For works whose claims are disputed or superseded, explain the distinction between enduring historical importance and present-day reliability rather than silently conflating them.

Reassess both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today orders against the supported broad pool. Explain major changes and differences between the views, preserve original publisher positions and previous versions, and leave personal numerical criteria, weights and scores unset.

Resolve essays versus book-length works, selected writings versus whole works, multi-volume identities and overlapping editions. Record English-edition and media gaps without allowing missing enrichment to decide inclusion or order.
nonfiction-all-time.desired_scope: Approximately 250 nonfiction books across subjects and worldwide traditions, with corrected source dependencies and a more explicit comparative basis. Keep unsupported expansion in a candidate queue instead of padding the published proposal.

philosophy-books-all-time.issue_summary: The current 250-entry initial selection has 256 ledger records, 235 flagged eligible and 100 distinct eligible source IDs in current entry references. There are 154 single-reference entries; 130 entries cite only Goodreads URLs, and 142 standing explanations use a generic 'Included in the reviewed' formulation. Eighty-five eligible records retain generic automatic-review notes without current entry links. Topic popularity lists and general thinker references can be useful discovery evidence, but do not by themselves justify work-level comparative standing across philosophy.
tasks: Review every supplied work for philosophy-book scope and identity. Distinguish primary philosophical works, secondary introductions, adjacent literature, compilations and popular self-help, recording borderline decisions and overlap instead of silently excluding or merging items.

Audit the Goodreads-only support and recurring mind, political, feminist and Stoic topic-list families. Preserve their reader-reception evidence while checking list scope, dependencies and actual candidate inclusion; do not automatically reject community evidence or turn nomination frequency into philosophical merit.

Review the 85 eligible records with generic automatic-review notes and propose documented corrections. Distinguish actual substantive consultation from returned-page length, title matches and supplied eligibility flags; preserve previous records and source IDs.

Strengthen work-specific evidence where current references discuss only a philosopher generally or provide a list appearance. Use relevant scholarship, specialist institutions, substantial criticism, independent editorial selections and substantive reader discussions to explain the particular work's contribution, reception and important objections.

Check coverage across major philosophical traditions, historical periods and branches, using relevant existing evidence first and focused new consultation for meaningful gaps. Normalize translation variants and collected works; neither one encyclopedia page nor an entire unrelated source ledger should be copied across every book by an author.

Replace generic standing explanations for consequential or weakly supported placements with short source-backed comparisons. Reassess the preserved leading group and topic-list-derived tail against the broad pool, identifying dependence and uncertainty rather than assigning artificial numerical merit values.

Return both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today proposals with explained differences. Difficulty may affect the recommended approach, but is not an automatic deduction from reading value. Keep personal criteria, weights and numerical scores unset, and keep exact source positions separate.

Record English availability, translation and edition issues, and missing images as follow-up tasks. Do not shrink the intellectually supported pool to works with completed edition or media records, and preserve reasons for proposed additions, exclusions or replacements.
philosophy-books-all-time.desired_scope: Approximately 250 philosophical books or clearly identified book-length philosophical works, across traditions and branches. Improve support, work identity and both qualitative orders rather than expanding merely to meet a number.

philosophers-all-time.issue_summary: This target remains a 23-person initial selection with 100 eligible ledger records and 38 distinct eligible source IDs in current entry references. Its central problem is incomplete breadth, not a poor source-to-entry ratio. The saved method still says Wiredu and Xunzi await suitable images, which conflicts with the later instruction that missing images must not exclude major candidates. The existing small group's positions must be reconsidered against an expanded comparison pool rather than treated as settled global ranks.
tasks: Begin with all 23 existing people, both editorial orders and the complete target-specific ledger. Identify supported candidates already present in the supplied evidence, then use full relevant surveys, substantial histories of philosophy, specialist references and established selections to build a broader comparison pool efficiently.

Expand across documented philosophical traditions, historical periods and branches using meaningful person-specific evidence. Record the scope basis for religious thinkers, political theorists, interdisciplinary writers and disputed philosopher classifications; do not infer membership from fame or force numerical demographic quotas.

Review the recorded pending status of Wiredu and Xunzi and any other image-dependent omissions. Include supported candidates on intellectual and scope grounds, retaining missing or uncertain portraits as separate tasks; historical depictions must be labelled honestly.

Distinguish evidence about a thinker's originality, influence and reception from evidence about individual books, public popularity or syllabus frequency. A philosopher's proposed rank must not be an unexplained average of their books' positions.

Audit the supplied ledger's actual target relevance, independence and consultation evidence before claiming its eligible total as verified research. Reuse substantive existing records and consult new sources where they resolve candidate or comparison gaps; do not demand a fixed number of sources per person or an arbitrary new-source quota.

Reassess the original 23 alongside the full supported pool and propose both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today views. Explain consequential placements, uncertainty and differences between views, including sensible starting works where supported; leave personal numerical criteria, weights and scores unset.

Return the expanded supported proposal plus a clear continuation queue for unresolved people. Preserve all prior identities, source IDs, evidence and positions in the change history, and do not invent candidates, consultation claims or confident ranks to reach the intended size.
philosophers-all-time.desired_scope: Expand from 23 toward approximately 250 philosophers worldwide only where there is meaningful support and coherent scope. Deliver the largest well-supported useful update with explicit remaining gaps if approximately 250 is not yet defensible; do not pad or let portrait availability limit membership.

history-books-all-time.issue_summary: The current initial selection has 234 entries and 200 ledger records. Of 155 flagged eligible records, 33 distinct sources are cited by current entries and the other 122 retain generic automatic-review notes. There are 159 entries whose references are exclusively Goodreads, 104 single-reference entries, and generic standing explanations throughout. General, popular, American and medieval topic lists supply substantial portions of the pool. A worldwide all-time history synthesis therefore needs stronger source qualification, scope balance and comparative reasoning; the existing total is not proof of 155 substantive independent assessments.
tasks: Audit all supplied source records, prioritizing those supporting current candidates and the 122 eligible generic automatic-review records. Distinguish examined relevant content from navigation, page metadata, title-only appearances, dependent copies and unexamined leads; propose explicit eligibility corrections without deleting the originals.

Identify the actual independent sources behind the current Goodreads-heavy pool and preserve original list scope and positions. Separate popularity, nominations and topical list membership from scholarly historical assessment, and avoid treating multiple pages on one platform as independent agreement by default.

Clarify and consistently apply the boundary of history books: distinguish historical scholarship and narrative history from historical fiction, primary sources, memoir, biography, historiography and adjacent social science. Preserve borderline records for explicit decisions instead of silently moving or removing them.

Check worldwide, chronological and thematic coverage so American and medieval topic-list availability does not accidentally define the all-time ranking. Use targeted scholarly reviews, major historiographical discussions, specialist institutions, independent editorial selections and substantive reader responses to address meaningful gaps without artificial regional or source quotas.

Replace generic placement rationales with concise book-specific evidence for historical contribution, methods, reception and significant criticism. Distinguish a work's enduring historiographical influence from whether its arguments remain reliable; explain controversies and superseded claims where material.

Reassess all supported candidates in both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today views. State a defensible qualitative method rather than equating website-domain breadth or URL recurrence with quality; preserve exact source positions, prior versions and uncertainty, and keep personal numerical scores unset.

Consider well-supported omissions and normalize translations, multi-volume histories, abridgments and overlapping editions. Work toward the broad intended size without padding, and track English-edition and image gaps separately from inclusion and merit.
history-books-all-time.desired_scope: A worldwide history-books synthesis around 250 supported entries, improving the current 234-entry pool and both qualitative orders. Prioritize evidence and scope repairs; retain an explicit queue if remaining additions or classifications are unresolved.

poetry-all-time.issue_summary: The current initial selection has 162 entries and 200 ledger records. Of 177 flagged eligible records, 38 distinct sources are cited by current entries and the other 139 retain generic automatic-review notes. Eighty-nine entries cite only Goodreads URLs, 63 have one reference, and standing explanations are generic throughout. Best Poetry, Popular Poetry and Best Epic Poetry lists dominate. Individual poems, collections, complete works and anthologies also require explicit identity and scope distinctions before their comparative positions can be interpreted coherently.
tasks: Classify every current entry by form and identity: individual poem, book-length poem or epic, author collection, selected/complete works, or multi-author anthology. Record overlaps between a poem and collections containing it. Make an explicit recommendation for a coherent poetry-work scope or clearly labelled form groups; do not silently collapse the categories or erase current records.

Audit the 139 eligible records with generic automatic-review notes and the 38 currently cited sources. Distinguish substantive examined content from page metadata, navigation, title appearances, dependent lists and unexamined leads; return supported eligibility corrections while preserving historical records and source IDs.

Assess the independence and scope of the dominant Goodreads list families, retaining their reader-reception value without equating nominations with critical agreement. Keep anthologies, educational collections and reading sequences distinct from ranked merit lists and preserve original positions only where they actually exist.

Use targeted poetry criticism, scholarship, specialist institutions, substantial editorial selections and meaningful reader discussion to strengthen weak entries and missing traditions. Consider translated and non-English poetry through sources you can reliably understand, without claiming worldwide coverage from a small set of English-language popularity lists.

Develop concise candidate-specific inclusion and comparison notes appropriate to each form. Explain the limits of comparing an individual lyric with a lifetime collected edition or epic; where a single order remains defensible, state the method and uncertainty rather than letting edition size or website recurrence determine merit.

Propose both critical-standing/enduring-influence and reading-value-today views, with reasons for major differences and significant changes. Preserve previous positions and source provenance, avoid automatic penalties for difficulty, and leave personal numerical criteria, weights and scores unset.

Identify consequential translation choices, collection contents and edition mismatches where possible. Keep missing covers, portraits and detailed metadata in a separate queue, and expand the supported pool only after the form boundary is explicit; do not add duplicate contents merely to approach the intended size.
poetry-all-time.desired_scope: Clarify the existing mixed poetry forms first, then improve and expand the 162-entry pool toward roughly 250 only if the chosen scope and meaningful evidence support it. Prefer an honest, coherent shorter update to padding with overlapping poems, collections or anthology editions.
